newsitem.title: CANADA: Potash Corp fueled by product pricing.
newsitem.headline: Potash Corp fueled by product pricing.

text.p: Shares of Potash Corp of Saskatchewan Inc jumped in Toronto and New York on Monday as investors rushed to cash in on strong prices for potash and nitrogen, two of the fertilizer giant's main products.
Potash stock on the Toronto Stock Exchange climbed C$3.25 to C$120 on thin volume of 39,033 shares. In New York, Potash gained 2-1/5 to trade at 88-1/4 with 438,000 shares trading.
David Davidson, analyst with CIBC Wood Gundy, said strength in product pricing has led to Potash Corp's stock price approaching predictions for spring 1997.
He had expected the stock to approach US$95 within the next three months.

"It's one of the more liquid fertilizer stocks in the U.S. -- and the biggest one -- and when you have people chasing a momentum stock like Potash can be at times, I would not at all be surprised if the stock exceeds the price," Davidson said.
The company served notice at the end of last year that it intended to raise potash fertilizer prices by seven to 10 percent in February, an increase that industry watchers expect will stick.
Potash Corp was also riding the wave of strong ammonia prices, which at US$250 per short ton in the U.S. Midwest were much higher than last year, Davidson said.
The company's US$1.18 billion purchase of Arcadian Corp made it a top global producer of nitrogen-based fertilizer and very sensitive to ammonia prices, he said.
CIBC Wood Gundy in December dropped its recommendation for Potash Corp to "accumulate" from "strong buy," mostly because of the runup in the company's stock price.
Davidson said, however, that trading in fertilizer stocks is traditionally strong in the months leading up to the spring planting season.

"March is generally the time when these stocks peak," he said. "The reason is that a lot of people want to lay off the risk of weather...in March, there is a tendency to correct." ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
